note: A live end-to-end build: the requirements panel, then every build stage, on real models. All text was written by models.
brief: Price a promotion where a 10% discount and a buy-3-get-1-free offer can both apply to the same product line. Return the line total.
facts: A line has sku, units and unitPrice. Made-up example: 8 units at 5.00 normal price is 40.00.

route.text:
How risky is this change?  → medium · 0.92  (low 0.05 · medium 0.92 · high 0.03)
Does it touch personal, health or financial data?  → no · 0.75
Can one model handle it safely on its own?  → yes · 0.57
Decision: the full panel. Two independent models check each other, and a person signs off at every gate.
A low-risk request, such as fixing a typo, would go to one model and a person, at a fraction of the cost.

panel.draftA:
REQ-1 Input is one line with sku, units (whole number, 0 or more) and unitPrice (0 or more). Output is the line total in the same currency, rounded once at the end to 2 decimals. The rounding rule is not in the brief; assume half-up and confirm with the requester.
REQ-2 Buy-3-get-1-free: free units = floor(units / 4), counted within the units on the line, so every 4th unit is free. This reading is an assumption; the brief does not say whether the free unit is part of the line or added on top.
REQ-3 When both promotions apply, line total = (units - free units) x unitPrice x 0.90. The 10% discount applies only to paid units. This order is an assumption to confirm: discounting the gross first and then removing free units at full price gives a different, lower total (26.00 instead of 27.00 in AC-1).
REQ-4 If units < 4, only the 10% discount applies. Reject negative units or a negative unitPrice with an error, and return no total.
AC-1 8 units at 5.00 (normal 40.00): free = 2, paid = 6, 6 x 5.00 = 30.00, x 0.90 = 27.00 line total.
AC-2 3 units at 5.00: free = 0, 15.00 x 0.90 = 13.50 line total.
AC-3 7 units at 5.00: free = 1, paid = 6, line total 27.00. This is the same as 8 units, which confirms the 4th unit must be on the line to be free.
AC-4 0 units at 5.00 returns 0.00. Units of -1 is rejected with an error.
panel.draftB:
REQ-1: A line has sku, units and unitPrice, and a 10% discount and buy-3-get-1-free may both apply to that same line.
REQ-2: Normal price before either offer is units times unitPrice.
REQ-3: Buy-3-get-1-free charges three units and waives one unit in each complete set of four; leftover units are charged.
REQ-4: After free units are removed, apply 10% to the paid amount and return that figure as the line total.
AC-1: 8 units at 5.00 have normal price 40.00, two free units and six paid units, paid amount 30.00, line total 27.00.

findings.title: False confirmation of free-unit rule
findings.detail: AC-3 says equal totals for 7 and 8 units confirm that the free unit must already be on the line. That equality only follows from the unconfirmed floor(units/4) assumption in REQ-2. It does not establish the rule.
findings.quote: This is the same as 8 units, which confirms the 4th unit must be on the line to be free.

reviewOfA.strengths: Worked totals match the stated formula, including the given normal price of 40.00 and the alternative stack of 26.00.

findings.title: No rounding rule for discount
findings.detail: Taking 10% off can produce fractions of a cent, for example 0.045 for one unit at 0.05. The draft does not say when to round, to how many decimals, or how. Different implementations could then return different line totals.
findings.quote: apply 10% to the paid amount and return that figure as the line total

findings.title: No leftover or small-quantity criteria
findings.detail: AC-1 only tests a multiple of four. Add criteria for leftover units, for example 7 units at 5.00: 1 free, 6 paid, 30.00, total 27.00. Also add one for fewer than four units and one for zero or invalid units.

reviewOfB.strengths: AC-1 is arithmetically correct and traceable: 8 x 5.00 = 40.00, two free units leave six paid at 30.00, and 10% off gives 27.00.

merge.document:
REQ-1 Input is one line with sku, units (whole number, 0 or more) and unitPrice (0 or more). Both the 10% discount and buy-3-get-1-free may apply to the same line. The normal price is units x unitPrice. Output is the line total in the same currency, rounded once at the end to 2 decimals. The rounding rule is not in the brief; assume half-up and confirm with the requester. For example, 1 unit at 0.05 gives 0.045, which rounds to 0.05.
REQ-2 Buy-3-get-1-free: free units = floor(units / 4), counted within the units on the line. One unit is waived in each complete set of four, and leftover units are charged. This reading is an assumption; the brief does not say whether the free unit is part of the line or added on top.
REQ-3 When both promotions apply, line total = (units - free units) x unitPrice x 0.90. The 10% discount applies only to paid units. This order is an assumption to confirm. Discounting the gross first and then removing free units at full price gives a lower total (26.00 instead of 27.00 in AC-1).
REQ-4 If units < 4, only the 10% discount applies. Reject negative units or a negative unitPrice with an error, and return no total.
AC-1 8 units at 5.00 (normal 40.00): free = 2, paid = 6, 6 x 5.00 = 30.00, x 0.90 = 27.00 line total.
AC-2 3 units at 5.00: free = 0, 15.00 x 0.90 = 13.50 line total.
AC-3 7 units at 5.00: free = 1, paid = 6, 30.00 x 0.90 = 27.00 line total. This follows the REQ-2 assumption and is not evidence for it.
AC-4 0 units at 5.00 returns 0.00. Units of -1 is rejected with an error.
AC-5 1 unit at 0.05: 0.05 x 0.90 = 0.045, which rounds half-up to 0.05 line total.
merge.keptFromA: I kept draft A's full structure: its input and validation rules, its explicit assumptions on rounding, free-unit counting and stacking order, and its worked criteria AC-1 to AC-4, all of which I rechecked.
merge.keptFromB: I kept draft B's explicit statement that both offers apply to the same line, its definition of the normal price as units x unitPrice, and its wording that leftover units outside complete sets of four are charged.

resolutions.note: AC-3 no longer claims that the equal totals confirm the free-unit rule. It now says the result follows from the REQ-2 assumption and is not evidence for it.
REQ-1 sets one rounding step at the end, to 2 decimals, assuming half-up pending confirmation. AC-5 tests the 0.045 case and expects 0.05.
Added criteria for leftover units (AC-3, 7 units gives 27.00), for fewer than four units (AC-2, 3 units gives 13.50), and for zero and invalid units (AC-4).

findings.title: Example skips discount math
findings.detail: One unit at 0.05 has a normal price of 0.05, not 0.045. The value 0.045 appears only after the 10 percent discount (0.05 x 0.90). The example states a wrong figure for those inputs.
findings.quote: For example, 1 unit at 0.05 gives 0.045, which rounds to 0.05.

finalReview.strengths: Acceptance criteria AC-1 through AC-5 recompute correctly, and 8 units at 5.00 is kept as a normal price of 40.00.

resolutions.finding: D-F1 · P0 · Example skips discount math
resolutions.note: Real issue: the REQ-1 example went from 1 unit at 0.05 straight to 0.045 and skipped the discount step. It now gives the normal price of 0.05, then shows the 10% discount (0.05 x 0.90 = 0.045) before rounding to 0.05. The final result was already correct, and it matches AC-5, so P0 overstates the severity. Nothing else was changed.

build.contract: priceLine(line) where line = { sku: string, units: number (whole number), unitPrice: number (in the line's currency) }. Returns { sku: string, normalPrice: number (units x unitPrice, unrounded), freeUnits: number (whole number), paidUnits: number (whole number), lineTotal: number (same currency, rounded to 2 decimals) }. Throws an Error whose message is "invalid field: <name>", where <name> is units or unitPrice, when that field is rejected; no result is returned in that case.

architecture.draft:
Component: one pure function priceLine(line) in a new module, with no I/O and no shared state; it follows the module contract exactly.
Steps: 1) validate; 2) normalPrice = units x unitPrice, unrounded; 3) freeUnits = floor(units / 4); 4) paidUnits = units - freeUnits; 5) lineTotal = round2HalfUp(paidUnits x unitPrice x 0.90); 6) return { sku, normalPrice, freeUnits, paidUnits, lineTotal }. Units < 4 needs no special case because freeUnits is then 0.
Validation: throw Error("invalid field: units") if units is negative, not a whole number or not finite. Throw Error("invalid field: unitPrice") if unitPrice is negative or not finite. REQ-4 names only negatives; rejecting fractional units follows the contract's whole-number rule and needs requester confirmation.
Arithmetic: compute lineTotal from a decimal or scaled-integer value, not binary floating point. In floating point, 0.05 x 0.90 gives 0.0449999..., which rounds to 0.04 and fails AC-5. Example: 5 cents x 90 / 100 = 4.5 cents, which rounds half-up to 5 cents, so 0.05.
Rounding: round half-up exactly once, at the end. The half-up rule and the discount order (applied to paid units only) are assumptions still to confirm, so keep each in one named constant or helper that is easy to change.
Data: input { sku, units, unitPrice }. Constants: DISCOUNT_RATE = 0.10, BUNDLE_SIZE = 4, FREE_PER_BUNDLE = 1. No persistence and no config files.
Checked numbers: AC-1 8 units -> free 2, paid 6, 30.00 x 0.90 = 27.00. AC-2 3 units -> 13.50. AC-3 7 units -> free 1, 27.00. AC-4 0 units -> 0.00; -1 units throws. AC-5 -> 0.05. Discounting first instead would give 26.00 for AC-1.
File fence (only these may change): src/pricing/priceLine.js (new); test/pricing/priceLine.test.js (new), covering AC-1 to AC-5 plus fractional units and a negative unitPrice. These paths are proposed; the real repo layout is not in the facts, so confirm them before building.
Out of scope: other promotions, multi-line baskets, currency conversion, and any file outside the fence.
architecture.review:
AR-1 · P2 · Floating-point failure claim wrong
  Binary 0.05 times 0.90 is slightly above 0.045, not 0.0449999..., so half-up still gives 0.05 and does not fail AC-5. Avoiding binary floating point is still sound, but this sentence states a wrong result.
Strengths: Paid-units pricing and the cents example match AC-1 through AC-5, including half-up of 4.5 cents to 0.05.
architecture.final:
Component: one pure function priceLine(line) in a new module, with no I/O and no shared state; it follows the module contract exactly.
Steps: 1) validate; 2) normalPrice = units x unitPrice, unrounded; 3) freeUnits = floor(units / 4); 4) paidUnits = units - freeUnits; 5) lineTotal = round2HalfUp(paidUnits x unitPrice x 0.90); 6) return { sku, normalPrice, freeUnits, paidUnits, lineTotal }. If units < 4, freeUnits is 0, so no special case is needed.
Validation: throw Error("invalid field: units") if units is negative, not a whole number or not finite. Throw Error("invalid field: unitPrice") if unitPrice is negative or not finite. REQ-4 names only negatives; rejecting fractional units follows the contract's whole-number rule and needs requester confirmation.
Arithmetic: compute lineTotal from a decimal or scaled-integer value, not binary floating point. Binary floats can land just below a half boundary: 1.005 is stored as 1.00499999..., so half-up gives 1.00, not 1.01. AC-5 in cents: 5 x 90 / 100 = 4.5 cents, which rounds half-up to 5 cents, so 0.05.
Rounding: round half-up exactly once, at the end. Half-up and discounting paid units only are assumptions still to confirm, so keep each in one named constant or helper.
Data: input { sku, units, unitPrice }. Constants: DISCOUNT_RATE = 0.10, BUNDLE_SIZE = 4, FREE_PER_BUNDLE = 1. No persistence and no config files.
Checked numbers: AC-1 8 units -> free 2, paid 6, 30.00 x 0.90 = 27.00. AC-2 3 units -> 13.50. AC-3 7 units -> free 1, 27.00. AC-4 0 units -> 0.00; -1 units throws. AC-5 -> 0.05. Discounting first would give 26.00 for AC-1.
File fence (only these may change): src/pricing/priceLine.js (new); test/pricing/priceLine.test.js (new), covering AC-1 to AC-5 plus fractional units and a negative unitPrice. These paths are proposed; confirm them against the real repo layout before building.
Out of scope: other promotions, multi-line baskets, currency conversion, and any file outside the fence.
architecture.resolutions: AR-1 applied: Removed the wrong claim. Binary 0.05 x 0.90 is about 0.045000000000000005, which still rounds to 0.05. The arithmetic line now gives a correct example of a float failing half-up: 1.005 is stored as 1.00499999... and rounds to 1.00. The scaled-integer approach and the AC-5 cents example are unchanged.

code.summary: Implements priceLine(line) as one pure expression with no I/O or shared state. Validation throws 'invalid field: units' when units is not a finite, whole, non-negative number. It throws 'invalid field: unitPrice' when unitPrice is not a finite, non-negative number. normalPrice is units x unitPrice, left unrounded. freeUnits = floor(units / 4) x 1, and paidUnits = units - freeUnits. lineTotal discounts paid units only and rounds half-up once to cents. That calculation uses exact BigInt decimal arithmetic, taken from the shortest decimal form of unitPrice, so binary-float half-boundary errors cannot occur. The constants DISCOUNT_RATE, BUNDLE_SIZE and FREE_PER_BUNDLE are named, and the two open assumptions each sit in their own helper: half-up rounding in roundHalfUpDiv, and paid-units-only discounting in discountedPaidCents. Checked by hand: AC-1 8 x 5.00 gives free 2, paid 6, total 27.00. AC-2 3 units gives 13.50. AC-3 7 units gives free 1, total 27.00. AC-4 0 units gives 0.00, and -1 units throws. AC-5 1 x 0.05 gives 4.5 cents, rounded half-up to 0.05. Still to confirm with the requester: half-up rounding, discount order, whether free units sit within the line, rejecting fractional units, and the proposed file paths. sku is passed through without validation, because the contract defines no error for it.
code.review:
CR-1 · P0 · Line total conversion throws
  whole is a BigInt, and BigInt plus a string throws TypeError in JavaScript. Every valid line, including AC-1 through AC-5, crashes here and never returns lineTotal.
Strengths: Free units are floor(units/4), the 10% discount applies only to paid units, and cent math rounds half-up once.
code.resolutions: CR-1 · P0 · Line total conversion throws declined: BigInt + string does not throw in JavaScript; the BigInt is converted to its string form and concatenated. Only mixing BigInt with Number in arithmetic throws TypeError. For AC-1, cents = 2700n, so whole + '.' + rest gives "27.00" and Number(...) gives 27. AC-5 traced: num = 1*5*9*100 = 4500, den = 100*10 = 1000, q = 4, r = 500, so it rounds half-up to 5 cents, giving 0.05. AC-2 (13.50), AC-3 (27.00) and AC-4 (0.00) also hold. Code is unchanged apart from a clarifying comment.

TC-4 · REQ-2 one free unit in each complete set of four · sku=SKU, units=4, unitPrice=5.00 → normalPrice=20.00, freeUnits=1, paidUnits=3, lineTotal=13.50

diagram.summary: A pricing caller sends one line (sku, units, unitPrice) to the new priceLine function, which validates it, works out free and paid units for buy-3-get-1, applies the 10% discount to the paid units with one half-up rounding step using promo constants, and returns the line total or a validation error.
